source_notes.finding: Each sandboxed tool's ToolDefinition.function_signature (from its JSON Schema) is rendered as an `async def name(*, ...)` Python stub plus TypedDict blocks. With the CodeMode default dynamic_catalog=True the catalog goes into the agent instructions as <pyai:context id="toolset:code_mode:catalog">, and run_code's description keeps only static prose (module list, no fs/env/clock). Observed text in out/P1.txt.

Every sandboxed tool is listed upfront in the catalog. Tools marked defer_loading stay off the wire until the local search_tools function (Tool Search) or a capability load reveals them; the catalog update is then appended to history, so the prompt cache survives. This is the path past 100 tools without every schema in the prompt.

MontyExecutor drives the REPL with feed_start/resume: each external call pauses Monty as a FunctionSnapshot, CodeMode dispatches it through Pydantic AI's tool manager in the host process, and resumes with the result serialized to plain JSON. Async calls are kept pending so asyncio.gather resolves them together (P9 201 ms for five 200 ms calls). Tool functions, their credentials and os_access stay in the host process, also with a remote worker.

Monty interpreter in a separate worker subprocess, no filesystem, env, clock or network unless os_access or mount is given. README claims Code Mode is safe in a webserver and IPython Code Mode is not. Probes agree for Code Mode: P3 not-defined, P4/P5 blocked, all 9 P12 attempts blocked at Monty's runtime even with the type checker skipped.

Printed text and the last expression both return, as {'output': ..., 'result': ...}; only one of them when the other is empty. The printed-output cap is 10 MiB and fires as a MemoryError, not a truncation marker.

What the harness adds over raw Monty: raw pydantic-monty 1.6.0 has no time or memory default (results/pydantic-monty.json P6 no-limit-within-120s, P7 hit 4 GiB), while CodeMode applies 30 s and 256 MiB unless resource_limits='unlimited'. It also adds the 100-calls-per-snippet budget and keeps Monty's 1000-suspension session budget, which cannot be disabled.

One REPL per agent run: variables persist across run_code calls in a run and start fresh in a new run unless repl_store is set. A time, memory or print-cap trip resets the session. `restart: true` lets the model reset it.

Runtime errors go back to the model as a retry: 'Runtime error:' + Monty traceback with file, line and message, plus a list of nested calls that already started (so the model does not replay side effects) and session-reset advice when a limit tripped. Type errors return 'Type error in code:' with the ty diagnostic before any code runs. Retries count against max_retries=3.

Type checking runs only on the first snippet of a fresh REPL that has tools; later snippets skip it. Tools registered with requires_approval=True and external tools stay native under the default selector, so approvals still pause the run. speculate and eager can start read-only calls while arguments stream. IPythonCodeMode in the same package runs a real IPython kernel with no sandbox (README table), not probed here.

surprises: The 10 MiB print cap does not keep output away from the model. X-print-cap printed 11 MB: Monty raised MemoryError at 10,485,760 bytes and reset the session, and the retry text still carried all 10,485,760 printed chars between [stdout before error] markers (10,486,097 chars total). Below the cap nothing is truncated (P2). The README (code_mode/README.md:686) says the cap resets the session but not that the printed text is still forwarded. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/X-print-cap.txt.

The ty type check runs only on the first snippet (_toolset.py:1429-1431). The earlier run of this probe saw P12 stopped by ty and could not tell whether Monty itself blocks the escapes. Rerunning each attempt as a second snippet shows Monty's runtime blocks all 9. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/P12.txt.

max_suspensions=1000 is per REPL session, so it caps a whole agent run, not one snippet. X-suspensions got 991 lookups through, then every later snippet in the run failed with 'suspension limit 1000 exceeded' until restart. An investigation agent that fans out to many lookups across run_code calls hits this ceiling. Evidence research/probes/pydantic-ai-harness-codemode/out/X-suspensions.txt.
One over the per-snippet budget fails the whole snippet: asking for 101 lookups in one gather ran 100 on the host and returned none of their results to the code.
time.time() and datetime.now() raise inside run_code unless os_access or os_policy is set, so the SPEC's in-sandbox P9 timing code cannot run; P9 times the lookups on the host.

The harness turns raw Monty's G2 and G3 failures into passes: raw pydantic-monty has no default time or memory limit, CodeMode applies 30 s and 256 MiB by default. results/fastmcp-codemode.json (also Monty-backed, MontySandboxProvider) did not exist when this was written, so no numeric comparison with it.
